items: Running typically begins between 1.5 to 2 years of age (Dulcan p.29).
Jumping typically begins between 2.5 to 3 years of age (Dulcan p.29).
Hand dominance and coordination begin to develop during toddlerhood (Dulcan p.29).
A child is able to stack two blocks at 18 months of age (Dulcan p.29).
A child is able to stack eight blocks at 30 months of age (Dulcan p.29).
Scribbling spontaneously begins around 18 months, and copying a circle is expected at 36 months of age (Dulcan p.29).
key_numbers: 18 months to stack 2 blocks (Dulcan p.29)
30 months to stack 8 blocks (Dulcan p.29)
36 months to copy a circle (Dulcan p.29)
2 years of age for running (Dulcan p.29)

items: Brain volume reaches approximately 80% of adult size by 36 months of age (Dulcan p.18, p.29).
Synaptogenesis rates are as high as 1 million connections per second in the early years of life (Dulcan p.18).
During the preschool period, children have little ability to sustain attention on a task and are easily distracted by irrelevant stimuli (StahlNeuro p.463).
Prefrontal cortex synapses rapidly increase by age 6 years, after which up to half of them are eliminated by adolescence (StahlNeuro p.463).
Theory of mind (ToM) or understanding of false beliefs matures significantly between ages 4 and 5 years (DSM p.671, Dulcan p.143).
Approximately 80% of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) fail the Sally-Anne false belief task (Dulcan p.143).
Basic understanding of gender identity and labeling is achieved by age 2 to 3 years (Dulcan p.567).
Gender consistency (understanding that gender remains stable despite changes in appearance or activities) develops between age 5 and 7 years (Dulcan p.567).
Intentional masturbation as a normal self-exploratory behavior can emerge around ages 2.5 to 3 years (Dulcan p.568).
key_numbers: 80% adult brain volume by age 36 months (Dulcan p.18, p.29)
1 million connections per second synaptogenesis rate (Dulcan p.18)
80% ToM task failure rate in ASD children (Dulcan p.143)
2 to 3 years for basic gender labeling (Dulcan p.567)
5 to 7 years for gender consistency (Dulcan p.567)
2.5 to 3 years for intentional masturbation (Dulcan p.568)

items: Preschoolers show cognitive egocentrism, meaning they are unable to perceive or understand viewpoints different from their own (Dulcan p.47).
Preschoolers display animism, which is the tendency to attribute lifelike intentions, feelings, and thoughts to inanimate objects (Dulcan p.47).
Moral emotions including shame, guilt, and pride typically develop between 18 and 36 months of age (Dulcan p.29).
Bedtime fears of darkness and imaginary monsters are developmentally normal during the preschool period (Dulcan p.310).
Anxious attachment styles assessed at 12 months can predict the development of anxiety disorders at age 17.5 years (Dulcan p.322).
For children under 5 years of age, oppositional defiant symptoms must occur on most days for at least 6 months to meet the diagnostic criteria for ODD (DSM p.525).
Reactive Attachment Disorder (RAD) and Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder (DSED) can only be diagnosed in children with a developmental age of at least 9 months (DSM p.296, p.299).
key_numbers: 6 months of most-day symptoms for ODD under age 5 (DSM p.525)
9 months minimum developmental age for RAD or DSED (DSM p.296, p.299)
18 to 36 months of age for moral emotions (Dulcan p.29)
12 months of age attachment predicting anxiety at 17.5 years (Dulcan p.322)

items: At age 2 years, only about 50% of a child's speech sound production is understandable to a stranger (DSM p.50).
By age 3 years, a child's speech should be mostly intelligible to a stranger (DSM p.50).
The gender ratio for speech sound disorder ranges from 1.5:1 to 1.8:1, being significantly more prevalent in boys than girls (DSM p.50).
Receptive language impairments carry a poorer clinical prognosis and are more treatment-resistant than expressive language deficits (DSM p.48, Dulcan p.162).
Social (pragmatic) communication disorder (SPCD) is rarely diagnosed in children younger than 4 years due to the developmental requirement for adequate structural language (DSM p.54).
Misarticulation of 'late eight' sounds (l, r, s, z, th, ch, dzh, zh) can be developmentally normal up to age 8 years (DSM p.51).
key_numbers: 50% intelligible speech at age 2 years (DSM p.50)
3 years of age for mostly intelligible speech (DSM p.50)
4 years of age minimum for SPCD diagnosis (DSM p.54)
8 years of age limit for normal late eight errors (DSM p.51)

items: Parallel play, where children play side-by-side with similar toys without active cooperation, typically occurs between 12 and 24 months of age (Dulcan p.29).
Early representational or symbolic pretend play typically begins between 24 and 36 months of age (Dulcan p.29, p.42).
Complex symbolic dramatic play, with rich imaginative themes and logical sequences of actions, begins at 30 months and older (Dulcan p.42).
Cooperative play involving shared themes and active division of roles with peers develops between ages 3 and 5 years (Dulcan p.43).
Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) show rigid, repetitive, parallel, and mechanical play rather than developing cooperative and symbolic play (Dulcan p.140).
key_numbers: 12 to 24 months of age for parallel play (Dulcan p.29)
24 to 36 months of age for early representational play (Dulcan p.29)
30 months of age for complex symbolic play (Dulcan p.42)
3 to 5 years of age for cooperative play (Dulcan p.43)

high_yield: Global Developmental Delay (GDD) is a temporary diagnosis reserved exclusively for children under age 5 years who are too young to undergo standardized IQ testing (DSM p.42, p.113).
Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD) is typically not diagnosed before age 5 years due to normal variation in motor skill acquisition (DSM p.86).
Encopresis cannot be diagnosed until a child reaches a chronological or mental age of at least 4 years (DSM p.403).
Enuresis cannot be diagnosed until a child reaches a chronological or mental age of at least 5 years (DSM p.400).
First-line treatment for ADHD in preschool-age children is behavioral parent training rather than stimulants, as validated by the PATS study (StahlKids p.15, Dulcan p.923).

To clinically evaluate attachment security, the quality of the caregiver-child reunion after separation is a significantly more reliable diagnostic indicator than the child's level of distress during separation (Dulcan p.28, p.49).

Preschoolers with unidentified language deficits are at highly elevated risk for developing externalizing behavioral problems like aggression and tantrums due to an inability to verbally express frustration (Dulcan p.53, p.362).

Under age 5, oppositional defiant symptoms must occur on most days for at least 6 months, whereas for older children, they must occur at least once a week, preventing the over-pathologizing of normal toddler behavior (DSM p.525-526).
